title: Fruity Blood Overdrive
notes: Distortion drive, filtering and post gain are coupled; qualify high-gain x100 behavior separately.

title: Fruity Chorus
notes: Delay, depth, stereo phase and crossover controls interact; qualify wet-only and crossover modes as state.

title: Fruity Compressor
notes: Threshold, ratio, gain, attack, release and type are documented; sidechain choices depend on mixer routing.

title: Fruity Convolver
notes: Impulse identity is part of the sound; editor, file and IR operations need guarded handling beyond parameter sweeps.

title: Fruity Delay
notes: Echo timing depends on Tempo and Steps; legacy baseline exposes named parameters but no host display text.

title: Fruity Delay 2
notes: TIME uses step:tick timing, OFS is directional, and repeated VOL labels must stay section-qualified.

title: Fruity Delay 3
notes: Tempo Sync changes Time units; delay model, feedback, diffusion, distortion and output sections should be qualified independently.

title: Fruity Delay Bank
notes: Eight repeated banks require bank-qualified names; NEXT routing, feedback and filter modes are unsafe to collapse across sections.

title: Fruity Fast Dist
notes: PRE, THRES and POST all affect level or distortion differently; algorithm A/B should be qualified as a selector.

title: Fruity Flanger
notes: Delay/depth/rate/phase shape modulation; dry, wet and cross gains include negative-infinity endpoints.

title: Fruity Flangus
notes: Stack count, spread and polarity-capable dry/wet/cross controls interact; physical units are mostly undocumented.

title: Fruity Limiter
notes: Compressor, limiter and gate sections share labels but have different semantics; limiter attack adds lookahead latency.

title: Fruity Love Philter
notes: Eight filter banks and articulator targets need bank/target-qualified names; pattern and editor actions are not blind sweep targets.

title: Fruity Multiband Compressor
notes: Low, mid and high bands repeat threshold, ratio, knee, attack, release and gain; crossover controls can create missing frequency ranges.

title: Fruity Parametric EQ 2
notes: Seven bands repeat type, slope, gain, frequency and bandwidth; LIN, HQ and monitor options affect latency or analysis state.

title: Fruity Phaser
notes: Sweep frequency range depends on the range selector; min/max depth and feedback should be guarded.

title: Fruity Reeverb
notes: Legacy reverb; baseline exposes named parameters but no host display text, so physical display qualification should remain conservative.

title: Fruity Reeverb 2
notes: Predelay tempo sync, mid/side mode, damping bypass and long tails need separate guarded qualification.

title: Fruity Soft Clipper
notes: Threshold and post gain jointly affect clipping and level; level-display editing is UI state unless exposed by the host.

title: Fruity Stereo Enhancer
notes: Stereo separation, phase delay, invert, pan and output controls require stereo-aware test material.

title: Fruity Stereo Shaper
notes: Matrix coefficients, phase/delay and sidechain difference routing can cancel or reroute audio; qualify one axis at a time.

title: Maximus
notes: Selected band context changes control meaning; envelope editors, lookahead latency and saturation modes need careful state handling.

title: Soundgoodizer
notes: Manual describes four Maximus-based modes and one amount control; current baseline exposes zero host parameters.

title: Transient Processor
notes: Split frequency/balance gate what attack and release shape; attack, drive and gain can raise peaks.

title: Gross Beat
notes: Time and volume slots, envelopes, MIDI triggering and rolling-buffer state are highly stateful; slot-note documentation needs runtime confirmation.

title: Tuner
notes: Monophonic visual pitch detector; reference, reactivity, bass and visual mode are not audio-processing controls.

title: 3x Osc
notes: Three oscillators use hierarchical mixing, coarse/fine pitch, phase, invert, AM and HQ controls; phase/invert can cancel signals.

title: FL Keys
notes: Instrument selection changes the response surface; pan, LFO frequency, overdrive and stretch should be qualified by sample/model context.

title: FL Slayer
notes: Deprecated in modern FL Studio; absence should not be treated as a qualification failure.

title: Morphine
notes: Four additive generators, morphing, resynthesis and editors create stored synthesis data; editor/import/randomize actions need guarded flows.

title: Ogun
notes: Additive harmonic masking, timbre impulse controls, resynthesis and XY modulation are interdependent and editor-heavy.

title: PoiZone
notes: Oscillators, filters, envelopes, LFO target amounts, arpeggiator and unison sections should be qualified by mode and target.

title: Sakura
notes: Physical-model excitation, string, damping, pickup and body controls interact strongly; avoid blind multi-control sweeps.

title: Sawer
notes: Oscillator, filter, unison, envelope, LFO, effects and arpeggiator sections are mode-coupled; source manual pages are beta URLs.

title: Sytrus
notes: Six operators can be carriers or modulators depending on matrix routing; graph/editor pages should not be treated as simple knobs.

title: Toxic Biohazard
notes: Six FM operators, matrix routing, filters, sequencer and effects are tightly coupled; source overview page is a beta URL.
